title: first_party is NOT shown on bounty objects, but the document promises it twice
detail: what_we_promise says the operator's activity is "labelled first_party on the profile, the listing and the bounty" and rules_enforced_in_code (line 219) says "first_party is shown on every profile, listing, bounty and leaderboard entry". GET /v1/bounties returns buyer as Party = {id, handle, trust_tier} (packages/api/src/modules/bounties/routes.ts:12 and :82); no bounty field carries first_party (grep first_party over modules/bounties/routes.ts: no hit). Only the opportunities view (world/routes.ts:25/72) has buyer.first_party. llms.txt line 170 repeats the claim ("agents, listings and bounties with first_party: true").
suggestion: Best fix: add the field. bounties/routes.ts:12 `const Party = z.object({ id, handle, trust_tier, first_party: z.boolean() })` and :82 `buyer: { id: b.buyerAgentId, handle: ..., trust_tier: ..., first_party: p?.firstParty ?? false }`. Until then reword both sentences to "labelled first_party on the profile, the listing, the opportunities feed and the leaderboard entry (a bounty shows its buyer, whose profile carries the flag)" and llms.txt line 170 to "agents and listings with first_party: true".

title: "Nothing ever flows into them from a job with another agent" is false for souk-services
detail: The note is attached to every first_party agent, including souk-services, which SELLS reference services (extract-web, validate-json, translate, ...) and receives USDC into its own wallet from third-party buyers (ADR-23 §1 and Umsetzung: "eigene Empfangs-Wallet"; packages/agents/src/index.ts:53 SellerRuntime). A buyer who pays souk-services and then reads this sentence sees the document contradicted by its own transaction.
suggestion: Replace the note with: "Every bounty, first purchase and sandbox faucet drip leaves the desk wallet (souk-bounties) and is visible on the explorer. souk-services is a seller and receives payments for the services it sells, like any other seller; on live it is never paid by another first_party agent (409 first_party_self_dealing). The faucet spends our own testnet money, not a balance held for anyone." Or attach a per-agent note: role: "pays" for the desk, role: "sells" for souk-services.

title: verify text cites changelog 0.3.8 for "3.5 USDC paid on-chain", but the changelog entry says nothing about a payment
detail: The verify string reads "Changelog 0.3.8 (wallet binding, reported by an outside agent, fixed and deployed the same day, 3.5 USDC paid on-chain)". packages/api/src/modules/meta/routes.ts:33 (0.3.8) only says the signature is now verified and names veriton; no amount, no payment, no hash. The fact itself is true (docs/STATUS.md:133: 3.5 USDC to veriton, tx 0x7be562c4d8a12ea6b6927745dd0f8d99bbddbc0d3f3b6cbde488d1b0530ae1f1 on Base) but the document points the reader at a source that does not contain it.
suggestion: Either extend the 0.3.8 changelog entry: "... (reported by the outside agent veriton through the security bounty; fixed and deployed the same day; the 3.5 USDC bounty was paid on Base after the fix, tx 0x7be562c4d8a12ea6b6927745dd0f8d99bbddbc0d3f3b6cbde488d1b0530ae1f1)", or change the verify string to name the transaction and explorer link directly: "Changelog 0.3.8 for the fix; the payment: https://basescan.org/tx/0x7be562c4d8a12ea6b6927745dd0f8d99bbddbc0d3f3b6cbde488d1b0530ae1f1 (3.5 USDC from the desk wallet to the reporter)".

title: verify names GET /v1/messages, an endpoint that does not exist
detail: The read-back promise lists "/v1/messages" as the call to check. There is no such route: messaging lives at GET /v1/threads, GET /v1/threads/{id} and GET /v1/threads/{id}/messages (packages/api/src/modules/messaging/routes.ts:134, :175, :192), plus GET /v1/inbox. An agent following the verify instruction gets 404.
suggestion: Replace "/v1/messages" with "/v1/threads and /v1/threads/{id}/messages" in the verify string (and in the claim text say "threads and messages").

title: "wallet changes refuse API keys" overstates what the route does
detail: The claim says "Key rotation, recovery and wallet changes refuse API keys and require a signature by your Ed25519 key". POST /v1/agents/me/wallet-address accepts a bearer API key (skill.md step 2 calls it with Authorization: Bearer as_test_...); only rotate-key and recover use requireSignature (agents/routes.ts:392, :417). A wallet CHANGE needs an additional Ed25519 proof in the body (agents/service.ts:273), but the request itself is API-key authenticated. The verify text below the claim already says this correctly; the claim does not.
suggestion: Claim: "Key rotation and recovery refuse API keys outright and accept only RFC 9421 signed requests; changing a bound wallet accepts an API key but additionally requires a proof signed by your Ed25519 key, so a leaked API key can neither take over the identity nor redirect income."

title: "We say hidden and deactivated, never deleted" is contradicted by the DELETE route text
detail: The enforcement string claims the platform never says "deleted"/"irreversible". The public OpenAPI description of DELETE /v1/agents/me still reads "Irreversible. Hides your profile..." (packages/api/src/modules/agents/routes.ts:481), its validation hint says "Deletion is irreversible" (:489) and the admin status route says "profile hidden; irreversible" (:518). ADR-32 decision 5 records that "irreversible" was to be replaced by "deactivation, not erasure"; llms.txt line 155 already uses the corrected wording.
suggestion: Fix the route texts: agents/routes.ts:481 -> "Deactivation, not erasure: hides your profile, revokes every API key and archives your listings. Jobs, messages, reviews and on-chain settlements stay as the counterparties' history and the handle stays taken; finish or cancel open jobs first (an unpaid sealed delivery still counts against you). Send {\"confirm\": \"<your handle>\"}."; :489 hint -> "Deactivation cannot be undone by you: all keys are revoked and listings archived. Send your handle to confirm."; :518 -> "profile hidden; deactivation, not erasure". Then the commitments sentence is true; until then drop the sentence "We say \"hidden and deactivated\", never \"deleted\"".

title: "no payment between platform-controlled wallets is ever recorded as a settlement" is not enforced in code and is false in the sandbox
detail: The only enforcement is assertNoFirstPartySelfDealing at job/bounty creation, and it returns early unless env === 'live' (packages/api/src/modules/agents/service.ts:333). In the sandbox two first_party agents may trade and their settlements are recorded like any other. There is no wallet-level check anywhere in payJob. The document is served for env=test too, where the sentence is plainly wrong; on live the mechanism is the 409 at creation, not a settlement filter.
suggestion: Replace with: "on live, no job or bounty award between two first_party agents can be created (409 first_party_self_dealing), so no live settlement between platform wallets exists; the sandbox is free for demos and counts nowhere as trust (ADR-23 §5-6)".

title: working_on publishes the smart-contract seller bond, which the legal review marked needs_lawyer with no publishable wording
detail: research/trust-limits-2026-09-08.jsonl "seller bond in a smart contract" has verdict needs_lawyer and an EMPTY wording field, i.e. nothing is cleared for publication. ADR-32 puts the bond under "Nicht entschieden, an den Anwalt" and lists as working_on only items "ohne Rechtsfrage" (milestones, exposure limits, key history, build id, export). Listing the bond as a work item, even with promise none, is a hint of a funds-touching feature aimed at counterparties (the same species of statement the licence finding warns about).
suggestion: Remove the item {item: 'A seller bond held in a smart contract.'} from working_on. If a mention is wanted at all, put it into what_we_do_not_offer as a negation: {not_offered: 'a seller bond or any funds held in a contract', meaning: 'Nothing that would hold, lock or release money is built or decided; the risk-reduction we work on (milestones, exposure suggestions) touches no funds.'}.

title: "Security findings are fixed before they are paid, and paid" reads as an unconditional payment guarantee
detail: Payment of a security finding depends on the report being reproducible, on a human confirmation (packages/agents/src/operator/catalog.ts:156, runtime.ts:634) and on a limited bounty budget (ADR-23 §3, ADR-31 desk caps 50 USDC lifetime). The claim states "and paid" flatly; the limits file requires every positive claim to carry its limit next to it.
suggestion: Claim: "A valid, reproducible security finding is fixed before it is paid, then paid from the bounty budget while it lasts; the report stays sealed until the fix is deployed." Keep the verify and enforcement strings.

title: changelog 0.3.9 says "public transaction hashes"; hashes are disclosed to the parties, not published
detail: The 0.3.9 entry lists "what survives the platform (public transaction hashes, ...)". The commitments document itself states the limit (commitments.ts:163: "Hashes are disclosed to the two parties, not published"), and the limits file flags "every paid job has a public transaction hash" as an overstatement that ADR-32 decision 5 corrected to "a transaction hash both parties can look up". The same phrase is in llms.txt (packages/api/src/discovery/text.ts:167, Commitments concept line).
suggestion: Both places: "what survives the platform (transaction hashes on a public chain that both parties can look up, receipts and attestations that verify offline against the did:key inside them)".

title: llms.txt Commitments line repeats "public transaction hashes"
detail: Same overstatement as changelog 0.3.9 (see routes.ts:22 finding). GET /v1/payments/settlements is auth-only; GET /v1/stats and /v1/feed carry no hashes.
suggestion: Replace "(public transaction hashes, receipts and attestations ...)" with "(transaction hashes on a public chain that both parties can look up, receipts and attestations ...)".

title: llms.txt: "bounties with first_party: true" - bounty objects carry no such field
detail: GET /v1/bounties buyer is {id, handle, trust_tier} (bounties/routes.ts:12); only agents, listings, the opportunities feed and the leaderboard carry first_party.
suggestion: Either add first_party to the bounty Party schema (see the commitments.ts:178 finding) or write "agents and listings with first_party: true are operated by Agent Souk itself (a bounty shows its buyer souk-bounties, whose profile carries the flag)".

title: "We will not remove read access to your own records" is a bare forward-looking promise with no stated enforcement
detail: Every other item in what_we_promise names what enforces it ("Our word", "nothing but our word enforces the notice period"). This one states a future guarantee inside the enforcement field without saying that nothing enforces it, which is exactly the pattern the limits file asks to avoid.
suggestion: enforcement: "There is no one-shot export endpoint yet; portability is page-by-page. We will not remove read access to your own records; nothing but our word enforces that, so download as you go."

title: caps_live/caps_test are the source defaults, not necessarily the running caps; desk caps missing from caps_test
detail: desk_per_day_usdc 20 and desk_lifetime_usdc 50 come from DEFAULT_CONFIG (packages/agents/src/operator/runtime.ts:49) but packages/agents/src/index.ts:59 overrides them from OPERATOR_TOTAL_BUDGET_USDC / OPERATOR_DAILY_CAP_USDC, and the same operatorConfig is used for the test desk (index.ts:65 per env), so caps_test silently omits the desk caps that apply there too. The values match ADR-31 today; the labels present them as facts.
suggestion: Rename to default_caps_live / default_caps_test (or add note: "defaults in the public source; the running values are at running_configuration"), and add desk_per_day_usdc: 20, desk_lifetime_usdc: 50 to caps_test.

title: verify grep claim: evm-signature.ts also contains an EIP-191 message SIGNER, not only verification
detail: grep privateKey over packages/api/src hits packages/api/src/modules/payments/evm-signature.ts:30 privateKeyToAddress and :60 signMessage(message, privateKeyHex). They sign EIP-191 messages (used by tests) and cannot form a transaction, but "finds only signature verification and test helpers" is not what the grep shows.
suggestion: verify: "grep privateKey|mnemonic|eth_sendRawTransaction over packages/api/src finds only EIP-191 message helpers (verification, plus a message signer used by tests; neither can form a transaction) and test helpers; ..."

title: verify omits the eth_call in chain.ts used for EIP-1271 wallet signatures
detail: packages/api/src/modules/payments/chain.ts:235 issues eth_call for EIP-1271 isValidSignature checks during wallet binding; the verify text attributes eth_call to ERC-8004 links only. A reader who greps chain.ts finds four methods, not three.
suggestion: verify: "... eth_getTransactionReceipt, eth_blockNumber, eth_getBlockByNumber for payments; read-only eth_call for EIP-1271 smart-wallet signature checks and ERC-8004 ownerOf/tokenURI. No eth_sendRawTransaction in the package."

title: "upfront ... (trusted sellers only)" holds on live only; the document is also served for env=test
detail: assertUpfrontAllowed (agents/service.ts:~296) enforces trust tier 1 for upfront only when env === 'live'; the sandbox allows any seller. With ?env=test the sentence is wrong.
suggestion: upfront: "You pay before any work (on live only sellers at trust tier 1 or higher may offer it; the sandbox allows anyone). Your risk is ..."

title: "every 402 body demands the full price" - after a partial payment the body demands the remainder
detail: termsForJob (jobs/service.ts:~482) sets amount = price - recorded partials. The verify sentence is meant to show no deduction, but "full price" is literally wrong after a partial.
suggestion: verify: "grep fee over packages/api/src finds only documentation strings; every 402 body demands the price (minus partial payments already recorded) to the seller's own address, with nothing deducted."

title: fee notice inconsistent across surfaces, and "platform wallet" names a wallet the API says it does not have
detail: commitments.ts:174 promises a fee change "at least 30 days before it applies"; payments/routes.ts:179, discovery/text.ts:102 and changelog 0.1.0 (meta/routes.ts:140) say only "announced ... first". payments/routes.ts:179 also says "a separate payment to the platform wallet", while the document stresses the API holds no wallet key and no address of ours appears in job payments.
suggestion: payments/routes.ts:179: "The platform takes 0%. Any future platform fee would be a separate payment for the platform's own service, announced in GET /v1/changelog at least 30 days before it applies (see /v1/commitments)." Apply the same "at least 30 days" wording to text.ts:102; leave the historical 0.1.0 entry as is.

title: "MIT" licence stated without a LICENSE file
detail: The repository root has no LICENSE file (ls shows none) and packages/api/package.json has no license field; only packages/sdk/package.json and the plugin manifest say MIT. The verifiable-claims research notes that "open source" as a licence claim is currently unsupported.
suggestion: Add a LICENSE file (MIT, copyright holder and year) at the repository root and a "license": "MIT" field in packages/api/package.json, or change the README line to "Licence: to be published".

title: Desk reviews are labelled machine_generated only by client convention; the API does not enforce the public rule
detail: GET /v1/commitments lists under rules_enforced_in_code: 'reviews written by the desk carry machine_generated: true', and ReviewView says desk reviews are 'always machine-generated'. createReview() stores whatever the caller sends (default false). The flag is set only in packages/agents (firstbuy.ts:614, runtime.ts:854), a separately deployed service. Any desk review posted by an agents build that does not send the field (the currently deployed image if the API ships first, a retry from an older process, a manual curl with the desk key) is stored as machine_generated=false and stays wrong forever: the 0008 UPDATE ran once at migration time and never again. That is a false public label on a review and contradicts the commitments document.
suggestion: Enforce server-side in createReview: `const machine = machineGenerated || reviewer.firstParty === true` and store/emit that value (the Agent type already carries firstParty). Then the claim in commitments.ts:219 is true of the API itself. Add a test: a first_party reviewer posting without the field gets machine_generated: true back.

title: Trust tier T1 counts the platform desk as a counterparty and its payments as volume; thirdPartyPayingAddresses is computed but never used
detail: sideFromJobs now returns thirdPartyPayingAddresses, but recomputeReputation still gates T1 on distinct_counterparties, payingAddresses (all wallets) and volume_usdc (all volume). With the ADR-31 caps the desk alone cannot reach T1 (one wallet vs minPayingAddresses 3), but it supplies 1 of the 3 wallets, up to all of the 10 USDC volume floor (a single bounty award is 3-10 USDC) and several of the 5 completed jobs (two first buys per seller plus bounty awards). So a seller needs only two outside wallets paying dust to become T1, which unlocks live dispute-panel eligibility (disputes/service.ts evaluatorEligibility) and instant bounty awards (runtime.ts:405). ADR-32's own reasoning ('a purchase by us is not evidence of demand') is not applied here, and nothing public says the desk counts toward T1. Not a false statement today (docs say 'distinct paying wallets'), but an undocumented limit that contradicts the ADR's principle.
suggestion: Either use the third-party figures for T1 (parties = max(asSeller.third_party_counterparties, asBuyer.third_party_counterparties), paying = max(seller.thirdPartyPayingAddresses, buyer.thirdPartyPayingAddresses), volume = third_party_volume_usdc sums) and adjust the existing T1 test, or delete the unused thirdPartyPayingAddresses field and state in the trust_tier description (reviews/routes.ts:76, discovery/text.ts:166) that platform purchases count toward tier 1. Record the choice in ADR-32.

title: Rows the startup backfill failed on are served as '0 third-party counterparties' with a description that calls that 'only the platform bought'
detail: sideView(), listings/routes.ts sellerReputation() (`?? 0`) and world/service.ts leaderboard (`?? 0`, rank_value 0) all turn a missing third_party_counterparties into 0. backfillReputation() swallows per-row exceptions (`catch { errors += 1 }`) and only logs a count, so a row that throws at startup (e.g. categoriesOf/settlements query failing under a busy WAL, a bad row) keeps reporting third_party_counterparties: 0 and drops to rank_value 0 until that agent's next job outcome or review, while the schema text says '0 with jobs_completed > 0 means only the platform has bought from this seller'. That is a wrong public number for a real seller in exactly the window ADR-32 tried to close.
suggestion: Make the split honest when unknown: make the three fields nullable in Side/SellerReputation/LeaderboardEntryView (`null` = not yet recomputed) and pass the raw value through instead of `?? 0`; in leaderboard() fall back to distinct_counterparties for ranking when the field is null, or exclude such rows with a log line. In backfillReputation log each failure with agentId/env and the error (`log.warn({ err, agentId: r.agentId, env: r.env }, 'reputation backfill row failed')`) so a failed row is visible in the deploy log.

title: Toggling first_party on an agent does not recompute the counterparties' first/third-party split
detail: sideFromJobs classifies by the first_party flag at recompute time. setFirstParty() (POST /v1/admin/agents/{id}/first-party) changes the flag but recomputes nothing; backfillReputation() skips every row that already carries third_party_counterparties. So if an agent is flagged first_party after it has traded (or un-flagged), every counterparty keeps stale third_party_counterparties, third_party_volume_usdc and leaderboard rank until its own next job outcome or review; a seller paid only by a newly flagged desk keeps rank_value > 0.
suggestion: In setFirstParty, after the update, select the distinct counterparty ids from jobs where buyerAgentId or sellerAgentId = agent.id (both envs) and call recomputeReputation(env, id) for each (plus the agent itself); it is an admin-only, rare action so the loop cost is fine.

title: first_party_counterparties + third_party_counterparties can exceed distinct_counterparties when one wallet address appears on both a first-party and a third-party job
detail: addresses is the union, but firstPartyAddresses and thirdPartyAddresses are filled per job by the counterparty's flag, so an address paid on a first-party job and on a third-party job is counted in both. distinct = |union| while first + third = |first| + |third|. The Side descriptions say 'Of distinct_counterparties', i.e. a partition. Today it needs the operator wallet to be bound to a non-first-party agent (binding requires a signature, so only the operator could do it), so it is an edge, but it is cheap to make the invariant hold. Free jobs, refund netting and paid-vs-free precedence are classified consistently with the totals (checked).
suggestion: Derive the first-party figure from the partition instead of a second set: `third_party_counterparties = thirdPartyAddresses.size + thirdPartyIds.length; first_party_counterparties = distinct_counterparties - third_party_counterparties` (an address any third party paid from is third-party).

title: Startup backfill runs before the server listens and has no upper bound on wall time
detail: backfillReputation() recomputes every stale reputation row sequentially (about 6 queries each, including the T1 promotion path and syncTrustTier) before createApp()/serve(). It is idempotent and bounded by the row count, and on the current live database (a handful of rows) it is fine; but on a larger database a Fly health check can kill the machine before it listens, and a restart repeats the remaining rows. The scheduler is started after it, so no concurrent recompute in-process; two machines would each run it (harmless, upserts).
suggestion: Either start the server first and run the backfill right after serve() (rows are served with the null fallback from the sideView finding until done), or keep it before serve but document the expectation in DEPLOY.md and print progress every N rows so a long run is visible.

title: Retroactive label is truthful for the code paths, but relies on 'every review by a first_party key came from the desk'
detail: Checked packages/agents/src: the only review call sites are firstbuy.ts:614 and runtime.ts:854 (both the desk, both judge-produced or a canned automated text); the reference sellers in services/ never review. So labelling all reviews by first_party agents is truthful for anything the software wrote. The one gap is a review a human left by hand with a first_party API key during testing (cannot be told apart by the SQL). Migration mechanics are fine: ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN NOT NULL DEFAULT false is valid SQLite, true/false literals are accepted by libsql (0002 used the same form), the comment inside the second statement chunk is handled by sqlite3 prepare in the file-mode client migrate(), journal idx 8 / when 1788886745020 is ordered after 0007, the snapshot prevId matches 0007, and freshApp() runs the full migration chain in tests.
suggestion: Before deploying, run `SELECT id, env, comment FROM reviews WHERE reviewer_agent_id IN (SELECT id FROM agents WHERE first_party = 1)` on the live database and check that every comment reads like the desk texts; if a hand-written one exists, exclude it by id in the UPDATE.

title: The new tests do not cover the backfill, free jobs, refunds, the not-yet-backfilled fallback, or a mixed leaderboard
detail: Not exercised by the last test in reviews/routes.test.ts or meta/routes.test.ts: (1) backfillReputation() on a row written without the fields (insert a row in the old shape, run it, assert the fields appear and that a second run recomputes 0); (2) a free (price 0) job from the desk and from an outsider: first_party_counterparties must count the desk id, third the outsider id; (3) a refund on a third-party job: third_party_volume_usdc must net it exactly like volume_usdc; (4) sideView/sellerReputation/leaderboard on a row lacking the fields (today they claim 0); (5) leaderboard order with one desk-only seller (rank_value 0) and one outside-paid seller, and role=buyer with the desk present (should be listed with first_party: true); (6) a first_party reviewer posting without machine_generated (see the high finding; today it comes back false); (7) the 0008 UPDATE on a database that already holds first-party reviews (tests run it on an empty table only). Also checked and fine: meta/stats.ts is semantically identical to the old /v1/stats handler (only a now parameter was added); recomputeReputation is the only caller of sideFromJobs, so no path recomputes without the first-party set; the review.received event payload carries machine_generated consistently; the public feed and receipts do not render reviews, so nothing there misses the flag.
suggestion: Add the cases above; (1), (4) and (6) guard public numbers and would have caught the findings in this review.
